results.title: Section 232 Steel and Aluminum
results.content:
Proclamations 10895 and 10896 of February 2025, among other actions, applied the Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs to additional steel and aluminum downstream (or “derivative”) products, calculated either on the full value of the product or the value of the steel and aluminum content of the product depending on the HTSUS Classification. [...] The Proclamations also required that the Secretary establish a process to consider public requests for including new derivative aluminum and steel articles within the scope of the Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs. On April 30, 2025, BIS publicized a rule implementing the resulting Section 232 Inclusions Process. Submissions are accepted in two-week windows three times per year.

For more information on the requirements for filing, see: [...] On March 8, 2018, President Trump exercised his authority under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 to impose tariffs on imports of steel and aluminum articles to protect the national security of the United States. This decision followed Section 232 Investigations into imports of steel and aluminum led by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS).

U.S.-metal carve-outs. Derivative goods made exclusively from U.S.-melted & poured steel or U.S.-smelted & cast aluminum are not subject to 232 (document it; HTS 9903.81.92 steel / 9903.85.09 aluminum). See CBP FAQ and CSMS above.

 Line 1 (non-metal portion). Base HTS duty (Column 1 General) + any reciprocal (IEEPA) tariffs/AD-CVD.
